text:
Alex: Heads up — this morning ~09:15 PST we saw a backlog on us-west-2 GPU pool when low-latency (live) traffic spiked to ~2.8k r/s. Non-interactive sync jobs started queuing behind long-lived sessions and we hit latency SLOs.

Priya: Is this under the qlen-based admission policy? I thought live had priority configured.

Sam: It does, but the admission controller weights requests by token cost, not by connection lifetime. Long-lived streaming sessions hold concurrency slots and prevent short sync jobs from getting scheduled.

Jin: Can we try "slot-per-connection" for live sessions (1 slot reserved per open stream) or a soft reserve (N% of pool pinned for low-latency)?

Marta: We saw something similar last month. Fallbacking streaming to smaller quantized variants reduces latency but increases cost because of more tokens generated per answer.

ops-bot: alert: gpu-pool-us-west-2 saturation=85% -> throttling engaged

Alex: Proposed experiment: reserve 20% of effective GPU capacity on each pool for live traffic (config: `stream_reserve=0.2`) + preemptible short leases for sync jobs. Also add an "idle-kill" for streams after 30s of zero token activity. Thoughts?

Priya: We need dashboards first: per-pool active_stream_count, avg_kv_cache_ttl, preemptions/sec, tail latency (p99.9). Who can add panels?

Sam: I'll add Grafana panels. Also suggest token-bucket for live spikes: allow a short burst up to X requests for Y seconds, then throttle to reserve. If the bucket empties, degrade new streams to sync path.

Jin: Network note — some clients keep sockets open even when idle. Idle-kill at 30s might drop valid sessions. We should use an application-level probe (heartbeat) to determine true active clients.

Marta: +1 on reserve + token-bucket. Also instrument per-tenant priority so noisy tenants don't fully consume the live reserve.

Alex: Cost tradeoff: a 20% reserve increases effective cost by ~8% on pools with baseline util=0.75. We can mitigate with autoscale burst capacity, but that adds warmup lag and extra infra ops.

Priya: Runbook change suggestion: if pool saturation > 80% for >5m, trigger migration of low-priority sync jobs to quantized nodes in the cost-optimized pool. Who owns the migration script?

Sam: I'll take the migration script + dashboards. ETA: EOD tomorrow for a minimal automated migration (no rollout yet).

Jin: I'll prototype runtime changes: slot-per-connection admission + token-bucket limiter. Need Sam's metrics signal for the bucket refill.

Alex: Action items: Sam — dashboards + migration; Jin — runtime PR for slot/token experiment; Priya — update runbook; Ops — add canary toggles for the reserve in prod. Run for 1 week, evaluate p99 and cost delta.

Marta: Also add an event trace for preempted requests so we can correlate tenant->priority->preemption.

Alex: If regressions appear flip `stream_reserve` off. @ops-bot please create an incident notification if p99 > 800ms for 3 consecutive minutes.

ops-bot: noted. Incident alert rule created: gpu-stream-p99 > 800ms for 3m -> #incidents

Priya: Thanks — once Sam and Jin have initial patches we'll schedule a canary window and post the checklist in #eng-runtime.

Alex: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the week-long trial and decide on permanent admission policy updates.
